title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: For Yb(III) NIR CPL, glum of individual crystal-field components changes with temperature mainly because hot bands and Stark components overlap differently, not because the coordination geometry rearranges.
explanation: In enantiomeric [Yb(L^NHex2)3](OTf)3 complexes in PDMS, cooling to 77 K narrows 2F5/2→2F7/2 Stark lines and suppresses hot bands according to a Boltzmann population. Each MJ component has its own temperature-dependent glum, and the (R) and (S) glum curves remain nearly mirror images.
scope: Crystal-field-split Yb(III) NIR emitters dispersed in PDMS; the reasoning is expected to apply to other Kramers ions with overlapping Stark CPL.
conditions: Variable temperature down to 77 K; no significant structural change assumed.
caveats: This temperature mechanism is drawn from one cited Yb/PDMS study. It does not replace humidity or photonic-band-gap effects seen in other solid hosts.
